title: Paths to Equilibrium in Games
headline: Open finding: The stated bound of at most n profiles is false; the proof gives at most n transitions, or n+1 profiles.

work.title: Paths to Equilibrium in Games
work.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (NeurIPS 2024)

claims.label: Satisficing-path profile-count bound
claims.gist: Every initial profile has a satisficing path to equilibrium with at most n profiles.
claims.statement: The published text states that the path length is uniformly bounded by T(x_1) <= n, where T counts profiles in the sequence (x_t) from x_1 to x_T.
conditions: Finite normal-form game with n players.
A satisficing path is indexed by profiles x_1 through x_T, so the number of transitions is T-1.
claims.quantifiers: For every initial strategy profile in every finite normal-form game.

result.summary: The printed bound T(x_1) <= n counts profiles, but the proof yields at most n transitions, hence at most n+1 profiles. In two-player matching pennies, an initial condition requires three profiles.
result.witness: In matching pennies, start at x_1=(A,C), where player 1 is satisfied. Every admissible successor must keep player 1 at A, but no Nash equilibrium has player 1 fixed at A; termination within two profiles is impossible. A legal three-profile path is (A,C), (A, 1/4 C + 3/4 D), then the fully mixed Nash equilibrium. At the middle profile both players are unsatisfied, so the final move is admissible. Thus T=3=n+1.
result.argument: The paper indexes profiles beginning at x_1. Its construction makes at most n-1 growth transitions before appending one equilibrium profile. If the growth phase ends at profile index k, then k=1+s for s transitions, so k<=n; appending the equilibrium gives at most n transitions and T<=n+1 profiles. The matching-pennies witness attains this bound. Scope is limited to the printed profile-count bound. The qualitative finite-path existence theorem is not challenged, and no claim is made that an efficient decentralized algorithm computes the path.
not_claimed: The qualitative theorem that a finite satisficing path to equilibrium exists is false.
An efficient decentralized algorithm computes the constructed path.
result.repair_note: State at most n transitions, equivalently at most n+1 profiles; the proof's terminal profile index should be k<=n.
